data.long_meaning: The one who perseveres through hardship, a name given to Prophet Job in the Quran. Parents who choose Aiyyub usually hope their child will grow to embody patient and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Aiyyub belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Patient.”

in_arabic.name: أَيُّوب
in_arabic.meaning: أَيُّوبُ: الاسمُ المُشتقّ من الأَيُّوبُ، يُشيرُ إلى المُستَظلّي، المُحتَفظ، المُستَحسِن

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ayub" or "Job" in Islamic culture is revered as a symbol of endurance and resilience in the face of adversity. It is often used as a source of inspiration to remind us of the strength we can find within ourselves no matter how difficult our circumstances may be. In many Islamic communities, the story of Prophet Job is recounted as a reminder of God's mercy and protection during times of hardship.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Ayub" or "Job" holds great spiritual significance in Islam as it is associated with Prophet Job, who is considered a model of patience and submission to God. The story of Prophet Job is narrated in both the Quran and the Bible, and it highlights his unwavering faith and trust in God despite the unimaginable hardships he faced. Prophet Job's story teaches us the importance of relying on God during times of hardship and to trust that He will ultimately grant us relief and reward us for our perseverance.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Aiyub, derived from the biblical figure Job, symbolizes profound patience and unwavering faith in Allah during times of immense suffering and hardship. Like Job who was tested with great calamities, those named Aiyub are reminded to remain steadfast in their belief and trust in Allah's wisdom and mercy.

historical_references.reference: Aiyyub ibn Shaddad al-Qadi was the founder of the Ayyubid Dynasty in Egypt, Syria, and North Africa in 1169 AD. He was a Kurdish military commander who rose to power after Saladin's death.

Aiyyub Ansari (also known as Imam Hussain ibn Ali al-Aiyyubi) was a famous Sufi saint and the founder of the Chishti Order in India during the late 12th century. He is considered one of the most revered Sufi saints in South Asia.
